result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers cap line length well, make code scroll inside its own box, and hide the right column below 1100px. B adds a collapsible inline 'On this page' list, so the outline is still there on laptops and phones; A just removes it. A has the tighter grid: its middle track is the reading width and the header lines up with the shell. In B, the 72ch article sits inside a 1fr track, which leaves an extra gap before the outline at wide sizes, and its header does not share the layout's container. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers cap the text width, make code scroll inside its own box, and hide the right-hand column below 1100px instead of letting it drop under the content. A wins because it replaces the hidden column with a collapsible 'On this page' list at the top of the article, so readers on laptops and phones can still jump between sections; B removes that navigation entirely at those widths. B has the tighter grid: its middle column is capped at the text width and its header edges line up with the columns. A's middle column fills the space while the text is capped inside it, which can leave a gap before the right-hand column.
